X.note: The lane is strong: textured crumbling plaster, backlit haze, a bright harbour, and a clear leading line to the flag. The figures are small, stiff, faceless, and have no real shading. Several wear flat shako-style black hats, which look wrong for 1782. The one dark figure in the middle reads as a silhouette cutout. The crowd is sparse, so the lane feels staged and mostly empty.

Y.note: It has the same strong environment. The troops wear tricorn or cocked hats and red coats with white cross-belts, which suits the 1780s better. The dense column gives scale and a sense of a event. But the figures are clones with stick legs, mismatched proportions, and olive or tan lower legs. They overlap into a muddy clump and look like game assets or dolls. Some figures merge into each other, and the pointing arm on the right is odd.

why: The environment is identical in both, and Y's crowd of tricorn-hatted redcoats gives more life and a more convincing period read, even though its figures are more doll-like and clumped.
top_fix_for_weaker: Fix X's headgear: replace the shako-like black hats with cocked tricorns, and add more varied, properly shaded figures in the lane (garrison soldiers, civilians, carts) with realistic leg and boot proportions, instead of a few stiff, flat-lit silhouettes.
anachronisms_seen: shako-style tall black hats on soldiers in X
uniform stick-leg figures with olive lower legs reading as gaiters or skin in Y
very uniform shuttered windows and door frames, with no glazing or period ironwork
